A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedDisco study. Their complete main text, figures, tables, algorithms, equations, and Appendix A support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CNN training experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST and OPT-125M fine-tuning experiments on SST-2 and CB, including Figures 2–3 and Table 2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original training and fine-tuning results in Figures 2–3 and Table 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Sections 2.1–2.2 retain the same seed/scalar communication, forward-difference updates, model reconstruction, synchronization, and implementation variants. The revised estimator-bias discussion does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST and Fashion-MNIST image classification, SST-2 sentiment classification, and CB inference. No dataset, task, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: FedAvg for MNIST; FedAvg, FedCom, and FedAvg + Top K for Fashion-MNIST; and SGD and MeZO for the fine-tuning tasks.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same models, data partitioning, learning rates, optimizers, perturbation schedules, metrics, and training budgets. The vision experiments still use 100 clients with 10% participation; fine-tuning still uses three clients with two participating per round.

E4.justification: Figure 2 retains the same ablations of local-update count and perturbation count. The Fashion-MNIST perturbation-scheduling experiment is also unchanged, and neither version adds further robustness or error analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains identical mean curves and bands labeled as standard deviations. Neither version supplies additional experimental repeat counts, run-seed specifications, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 and Table 2 report identical results. For example, FedDisco with ten perturbations remains at 86.73% on SST-2 and 74.90% on CB, with communication costs of 3e5 and 1.2e5 respectively.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, convergence bounds, and Appendix A derivations remain unchanged. Both versions already account for finite smoothing parameters and smoothed-gradient bias; added expectation brackets in Equation 42 and punctuation do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The introduction reframes one theoretical contribution: v1 emphasizes avoiding MeZO's stated requirement that the finite-difference step approach zero, whereas v2 emphasizes handling biased forward-difference estimators and claims extension to unbiased central-difference cases, but not conversely. The principal communication and convergence claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Remark 3 changes the explanation of the theoretical distinction to estimator bias. Appendix A.4 replaces the assertion that MeZO's claim is not strictly correct with the narrower statement that Equation 39 does not hold for this paper's forward difference. The computational-cost limitation and proposed future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub code-access link in the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation descriptions and hyperparameters otherwise remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the linked repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same 58 references, but the relationship to MeZO is revised in the introduction, Remark 3, and Appendix A.4. The positioning shifts from correcting an unrealistic limiting approximation toward accommodating biased estimators.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the theoretical-contribution discussion and scattered grammar, terminology, and punctuation corrections, including in the appendix. The overall section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–3 retain their content and design. Limited reflow moves Figure 3 to the top of page 10 and brings the beginning of the conclusion onto that page; some equation delimiters are also clarified.

improvement.justification: The new code-access information and localized language and notation corrections modestly improve reproducibility guidance and readability. The MeZO comparison is reframed without changing the supporting derivations. Since the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged, and repository functionality cannot be established from the PDFs, the demonstrated improvement is limited.
